notes.teachingPoint: Explain the original proposal process and how its publication model differs from present BIP3.
Explain the revised process and licensing framework that BIP3 later replaced.
Separate editorial publication, document status, implementation, adoption and Bitcoin consensus; relate the workflow to BIP123 layers.
Explain height-based version-bit deployment and optional mandatory lock-in, contrasting BIP9 time-based timeout.
Explain parallel soft-fork signaling, threshold windows, lock-in delay and bit reuse.
Explain the earlier multisig transaction-exchange format and compare its collaboration role with PSBT.
Explain bare threshold multisig standardness and why script-hash funding later helped hide complex spending conditions.
Explain OP_EVAL as an alternative script-hash design and why evaluating supplied code differs from BIP16 verification.
Explain Base58Check script-hash addresses as the recipient encoding, distinct from BIP16 spending rules.
Separate protocol version from user-agent identification in the peer handshake.
Explain the alias-resolution proposal and contrast its naming/trust model with DNS Payment Instructions.
Explain committing to a redeem script, revealing it when spent and applying the second evaluation.
Explain OP_CHECKHASHVERIFY as an alternative to OP_EVAL and P2SH, with its distinct validation sequence.
Explain the alternative input/output layout using dataSig, scriptCheck and hashScriptCheck; Complete does not establish adoption.
Explain the alternative low-sigop multisig script patterns and distinguish them from bare CHECKMULTISIG standardness.
Explain the early payment URI design and the changes represented by its BIP21 successor.
Explain bitcoin: payment instructions, optional versus required parameters, and its successor BIP321.
Explain how getblocktemplate gives a miner block structure rather than just a header to hash.
Explain pooled-mining extensions to the block-template exchange, including pool constraints and submission.
Explain why duplicate transaction identifiers can overwrite unspent outputs and what duplicate protection checks.
Explain nonce-bearing ping/pong as liveness measurement, separate from peer capability negotiation.
Explain seed-derived key trees, chain codes, extended keys and the hardened derivation boundary.
Explain the proposed specialization of node roles and compare its service/trust assumptions with light-client designs.
Explain height commitment in the coinbase and its relationship to uniqueness and early version-based deployment.
Explain asking a peer for its mempool inventory, without treating that inventory as consensus or a complete network view.
Explain the earlier proposal for extensible custom-service announcements alongside modern peer feature negotiation.
Explain server-side Bloom matching, false positives and what the wallet reveals when it sends a filter.
Explain passphrase-encrypted individual private keys and the distinction from encrypting or sharing a wallet seed.
Explain entropy, mnemonic checksum, seed derivation and why the passphrase changes the derived wallet.
Explain the real subsidy-shift arithmetic fix behind the satirical account of endless future inflation.
Explain the hardened purpose field as a namespace for wallet conventions, rather than another derivation algorithm.
Explain purpose, coin, account, change and address levels, together with account discovery and its limits.
Explain the earlier cosigner-index P2SH multisig hierarchy and contrast it with later multisig conventions.
Explain deterministic timelocked fidelity-bond addresses and certificate signing as a costly identity mechanism.
Explain reusable payment codes, notification and derived payment addresses, contrasting Silent Payments scanning.
Explain multiscript multisig derivation and the script-type level in the wallet hierarchy.
Explain the dedicated hierarchy for P2SH-wrapped SegWit and distinguish it from native witness accounts.
Explain how a database lock limit became an accidental validation boundary in the March 2013 chain split.
Explain the proposed optical proof-of-work change and separate the authors energy rationale from established security properties.
Explain ambiguity between 64-byte transaction data and internal Merkle nodes and the proposed narrow consensus restriction.
Explain the broader cleanup package: timewarp, worst-case validation, Merkle ambiguity and duplicate-transaction handling.
Explain the proposed fixed-length version-message relay flag and its relationship to BIP37 optional relay signaling.
Explain peer rejection messages and their limited diagnostic role; source status does not guarantee present node support.
Explain the earlier collection of transaction-malleability restrictions and which ideas appear in narrower later proposals.
Explain peer UTXO queries, the information returned and the absence of a general trustless UTXO proof.
Explain absolute lock checking in Script and its relationship to transaction locktime.
Explain strict DER signature encoding as a validation constraint rather than a new signing equation.
Explain compressed-key sorting before multisig script construction so cosigners derive the same script and address.
Explain relative sequence-lock semantics and their dependence on the age of the spent outputs.
Explain lexicographic input/output ordering and the privacy/auditability rationale without calling it a universal wallet rule.
Explain merchant PaymentRequest, Payment and PaymentACK exchanges and their authentication assumptions.
Explain the MIME types used to identify Payment Protocol messages, rather than a separate payment mechanism.
Explain the URI link from a bitcoin: request to a BIP70 payment request.
Explain HTTP content negotiation for short payment-request URLs without requiring every client to implement all BIP70 messages.
Explain the closed extension allowing zero-value OP_RETURN outputs in PaymentRequests.
Explain encrypted out-of-band address exchange as an extension to the merchant Payment Protocol.
Explain asynchronous Payjoin using a directory, encrypted payloads and sender/receiver checks relative to BIP78.
Explain sender/receiver collaborative transaction construction and the checks required before accepting the negotiated payment.
Explain Bustapay as a predecessor collaborative-payment design, with its own construction and safety choices.
Explain the historical deterministic multisig hierarchy for non-colored voting pools and its relationship to BIP44.
Explain the corresponding colored voting-pool hierarchy and identify the extra convention instead of merging it with BIP80.
Explain the proposed dynamic HD key hierarchy and contrast it with fixed purpose/account path conventions.
Explain native P2WPKH derivation and its dedicated account hierarchy and extended-key encoding.
Explain deriving application-specific entropy from hardened BIP32 children, distinct from directly reusing a seed across applications.
Explain single-key Taproot derivation and the internal-key to output-key tweak.
Explain a descriptor/PSBT-era multisig derivation hierarchy and compare its recovery assumptions with BIP45 and BIP48.
Explain path templates and constraints for describing permitted derivation paths, rather than a new wallet derivation scheme.
Explain withholding chain codes and supplying per-input tweaks so a cosigner can authorize without wallet-wide scanning visibility.
Explain replacing historical activation logic with fixed buried activation heights after deployment.
Explain the lower-threshold signaling mechanism used to coordinate the existing SegWit deployment.
Explain checksummed codex32 seed encoding and optional threshold shares, distinct from a mnemonic passphrase.
Explain Testnet4 difficulty and block-storm mitigations as test-network rules rather than mainnet changes.
Explain the proposed Testnet5 difficulty changes and BIP54 rules from block one, contrasting Testnet4 and Draft status.
Explain the proposed Fast Merkle Tree construction and its use by branch verification; do not identify it with Taproot hashing.
Explain the historical taxonomy and proposed deployment guidance for soft and hard forks, separate from modern BIP workflow.
Explain setting a dynamic block-size limit through miner coinbase voting.
Explain a scheduled maximum-block-size growth proposal and its timing/limit rule.
Explain the simple one-time two-megabyte maximum-block-size proposal.
Explain scheduled block-size growth tied to the authors technological-growth assumptions.
Explain a feedback rule targeting average block fullness rather than a fixed limit schedule.
Explain the proposed consensus-driven size-retargeting mechanism and what participants can influence.
Explain proposed dynamic size limits responding to previous size and, in one variant, fee information.
Explain a transaction-volume-based dynamic block-size ceiling and contrast its feedback inputs with other proposals.
Explain the two-megabyte proposal together with its signature-operation and hashing-resource limits.
Explain the closed temporary consensus data-restriction proposal and distinguish it from older block-size increases.
Explain the service bit that advertises Bloom-filter support and makes it optional for serving peers.
Explain checking relative age in Script in combination with BIP68 sequence semantics.
Explain median-time-past as the monotonic chain clock used for time-based lock eligibility.
Explain the earlier MAST witness-program design and contrast its branch disclosure and validation with Taproot.
Explain the proposed block-at-height commitment for chain-specific replay protection.
Explain verifying Merkle inclusion inside Script using the BIP98 tree design.
Explain tail-call execution of supplied code and how it composes with branch verification; it is not Taproot execution.
Explain signatures that omit the exact spent outpoint and the compatible-state/rebinding use case.
Explain checking a predetermined transaction template hash through OP_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY and its commitment limits.
Explain proving control of credentials used in a prior payment, distinct from proving a new arbitrary message.
Explain the proposed URI request/response entry point for Proof of Payment.
Explain chain-qualified blockchain reference URIs and how they differ from payment instructions.
Explain the consensus, peer-service, API and application classification layers used by BIP metadata.
Explain the earlier deterministic script-template approach and compare it with descriptors and structured Miniscript.
Explain opt-in replacement signaling and policy conditions; a signal is neither a consensus rule nor a present network-wide promise.
Explain the privacy rationale and limits of conventional transaction shapes when inputs use heterogeneous script types.
Explain proof-of-reserves transaction construction and its PSBT field; reserve control alone is not proof of liabilities or solvency.
Explain portable alert/recovery transaction plans, timelocks and monitoring data without presenting the format as a new covenant.
Explain exchanging and confirming multisig setup records so all devices agree on the same wallet configuration.
Explain requesting direct header announcements rather than inventory announcements for new blocks.
Explain the proposed coalescing transaction and wildcard-input construction as a distinct closed transaction design.
Explain the closed committee-based BIP acceptance proposal and contrast it with publication without an adoption authority.
Explain per-peer fee-filter announcements as relay preferences, not transaction consensus limits.
Explain the proposed extensible transaction serialization and its malleability and format goals.
Explain generalized configurable version-bit voting and distinguish it from deployed BIP9 rules.
Explain Bech32 transaction-position references and why a chain position is a weaker locator than a transaction hash.
Explain legacy recoverable compact message signatures and their address-type flags, compared with generic Script-based BIP322 proofs.
Explain encrypted non-secret wallet metadata backups and why the payload must exclude private-key material.
Explain normalized transaction identities that remove signature scripts for hashing and contrast them with SegWit txids.
Explain witness separation, output programs, transaction identities, commitments and block weight.
Explain the earlier proposed witness-address encoding and its replacement by Bech32.
Explain the version-zero witness signature message, input amounts and hashing work reuse.
Explain witness-aware peer services, transaction serialization and block/transaction inventory requests.
Explain how witness commitments and resource accounting change the block-template interface.
Explain the closed LOW_S/NULLFAIL consensus proposal and distinguish its scope from deployed strict-DER and NULLDUMMY rules.
Explain requiring the CHECKMULTISIG dummy element to be empty, across applicable legacy and witness scripts.
Explain the flag-day mandatory-signaling SegWit deployment and its relationship to BIP9.
Explain the unused second SegWit deployment proposal and its guaranteed-lock-in design.
Explain the earlier peer-authentication scheme layered over BIP151, separate from v2 opportunistic encryption.
Explain the earlier encrypted-peer-transport design and its replacement relationship with BIP324.
Explain compact-block short IDs, local reconstruction and requests for missing transactions.
Explain proof-of-work connection-admission challenges as an anti-resource-abuse proposal, separate from mining and encryption.
Explain larger peer-address encodings for Tor v3, I2P and other networks in addrv2 gossip.
Explain Dandelion stem/fluff routing and its transaction-source privacy goal, distinct from encrypting a link.
Explain the peer protocol for fetching filters and blocks, including trust and omission limitations.
Explain compact filter construction with Golomb-Rice coding as the encoding paired with BIP157.
Explain pruned peers advertising a limited recent block-serving range without claiming full historical availability.
Explain the proposed exchange-rate API and distinguish external price information from on-chain amount units.
Explain the proposal to standardize satoshi/sats terminology without changing consensus denominations.
Explain Bech32 witness-address encoding and checksum rules; after BIP350 it remains the encoding for witness v0.
Explain PSBT key-value maps, transaction roles, offline signing information and version-zero construction.
Explain how contract hashes and payment_base determine non-hardened BIP32 path components and a derived payment address; distinguish this from a single additive pay-to-contract key tweak.
Explain the bits denomination of one hundred satoshis and its display-only scope.
Explain the proposed base-unit terminology redefinition and distinguish display language from changing UTXO values.
Explain the proposed WIF extension carrying intended script/address type, not a new recipient address scheme.
Explain the proposed invoice-address terminology for recipient identifiers and its distinction from reusable identities.
Explain the proposed block size/weight fraud proof and exactly which invalidity claim it could demonstrate to a light client.
Explain the collateralized debt-contract application of hash/time-locked transaction branches.
Explain the closed HTLC script patterns, preimage claims and timeout refunds without claiming a full payment-channel protocol.
Explain the proposed hashrate escrow withdrawal mechanism, slow miner decisions and sidechain-user trust assumptions.
Explain blind merged-mining bids and block-selection commitments, separate from BIP300 withdrawal control.
Explain Stratum extension negotiation and version rolling, not the entirety of either Stratum generation.
Explain the proposed reservation of sixteen header-version bits for general-purpose use and the later BIP323 alternative.
Explain modern bitcoin: instructions supporting payment-method choices while preserving applicable BIP21 compatibility.
Explain Script-based arbitrary-message proofs, virtual transactions and the exact control claim a successful proof establishes.
Explain the proposed twenty-four version bits for extra-nonce space and its relationship to soft-fork signaling allocations.
Explain opportunistic encrypted peer transport, handshake, packet protection and the limits of unauthenticated connections.
Explain Signet signed-block admission layered over proof of work and its coordinated testing purpose.
Explain Taproot wallet locktime/sequence behavior intended to blend anti-fee-sniping patterns across off-chain protocol transactions.
Explain n-of-n aggregate keys, two-round signing, tweaks and nonce discipline for BIP340-compatible signatures.
Explain constructing derivable extended keys from MuSig2 aggregate public keys and the fixed aggregate-key chain-code convention.
Explain portable wallet labels and references as non-secret metadata distinct from seed or descriptor backups.
Explain reconciling transaction-announcement sets between peers, distinct from transmitting transaction bodies.
Explain requesting and relaying unconfirmed ancestor packages and transaction batches through peer messages.
Explain stale-tip announcements, branch headers and data availability without altering best-chain selection.
Explain transaction compression, including optional potentially lossy outpoint references and required decompression context.
Explain the closed per-connection transaction-relay disabling proposal and its block-relay-only motivation.
Explain negotiating transaction relay by witness transaction ID rather than the base transaction ID.
Explain x-only public keys, Schnorr verification, tagged hashes and the exact message authenticated by a signature.
Explain Taproot key/script paths, output tweaks, control blocks and spending commitments.
Explain initial tapscript validation semantics, CHECKSIGADD, signature budgets and upgrade hooks.
Explain the closed mandatory Taproot deployment proposal using BIP8, distinct from Taproot spending rules.
Explain the closed specialized vault/recovery opcode design and its proposed replacement by BIP443.
Explain configurable transaction introspection hashes through OP_TXHASH and their composition with stack-message signatures.
Explain concatenating stack values in tapscript; Complete describes the BIP document rather than OP_CAT activation.
Explain checking BIP340 signatures against stack-provided messages, not necessarily a transaction signature digest.
Explain exposing the Taproot internal key to script and its role in the proposed rebindable-transaction package.
Explain the checksum change for witness versions one and above while keeping Bech32 for witness zero.
Explain the closed Private Payments code/notification design and compare its on-chain footprint with BIP47 and BIP352.
Explain static payment addresses, input-derived ECDH output discovery, sender requirements and receiver scanning tradeoffs.
Explain DNSSEC-protected TXT payment instructions and the separation of name resolution from human identity assurance.
Explain the proposed Merkle-root output without a Taproot key path; removing exposed keys is not a post-quantum signature scheme.
Explain the proposed migration/sunset policy and its explicitly unspecified prerequisite post-quantum signature proposal.
Explain PSBT version two construction fields and input/output mutability compared with the version-zero unsigned-transaction container.
Explain Taproot-specific PSBT input/output fields supported in both version zero and version two.
Explain PSBT pay-to-contract tweak fields that let an external signer apply the matching private-key tweak.
Explain MuSig2 participants, nonces and partial signatures carried in PSBTs of either supported version.
Explain proving that the same scalar relates two point pairs without revealing it, particularly for Silent Payment ECDH shares.
Explain Silent Payment sending fields and changed PSBTv2 responsibilities when outputs depend on the final input set.
Explain PSBTv2 fields for spending Silent Payment outputs and distinguish that workflow from creating such outputs.
Explain structured, analyzable script composition for P2WSH and tapscript and distinguish Miniscript from a policy or descriptor.
Explain descriptor syntax, key expressions, origins, ranges and checksums as wallet script descriptions.
Explain pk(), pkh() and sh() descriptor expressions for non-witness script constructions.
Explain wpkh() and wsh() descriptor expressions and their witness-script boundaries.
Explain multi() versus sortedmulti() as descriptors for ordered or deterministically sorted threshold multisig scripts.
Explain combo() expanding one key into the applicable collection of output-script forms.
Explain raw() script encapsulation and addr() address encapsulation, including information those representations do not recover.
Explain tr() descriptors with an internal key and optional script tree.
Explain multi_a()/sortedmulti_a() tapscript threshold expressions and their difference from CHECKMULTISIG-based descriptors.
Explain compact, reviewable account policies for constrained signers and how they instantiate output descriptors.
Explain multipath key expressions grouping receive/change or other corresponding derivation steps in one descriptor.
Explain musig() aggregate key expressions and their BIP328 derivation behavior inside descriptors.
Explain the closed binary descriptor container proposal and its metadata maps, distinct from textual descriptor annotations.
Explain sp() descriptors for Silent Payment key material whose concrete scripts also depend on sender inputs.
Explain operational descriptor annotations such as scan height and gap limit that affect recovery without changing generated scripts.
Explain topology restrictions intended to reduce pinning and improve replacement reliability as mempool policy, not consensus.
Explain a keyless anyone-can-spend anchor output made usable through standardness policy, not a new signature scheme or soft fork.
Explain extensible peer feature negotiation so new P2P features need not each consume a new global protocol-version threshold.
Explain the proposed generalized execution-cost budget and its relationship to current tapscript signature budgeting.
Explain the proposed new tapleaf version restoring disabled script operations and expanding resources subject to BIP440 budgeting.
Explain tagged, length-delimited commitments to a pair of stack values and why that differs from plain concatenation.
Explain dynamic contract-data commitments and future output restrictions through OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY, including vault applications.
Explain pushing a fixed transaction-template hash onto the stack and contrast it with CTV checking and TXHASH configurability.
Explain the joint deployment proposal for TEMPLATEHASH, CHECKSIGFROMSTACK and INTERNALKEY, not an independently specified fourth opcode.
Explain x-only public-key tweak addition inside script, distinct from doing a Taproot tweak outside script.
Explain themed sentence encodings and their BIP39 re-encoding step without adopting the authors memorability claims as proven.
Explain the proposed dust-disposal transaction/signature convention and assess privacy claims under its batching and linking assumptions.
Explain standardized deterministic ECDSA signing with low-r grinding and low-s normalization, distinct from consensus validity rules.
